title: 48188 is a SHARED engine port - /comfy/start refuses the app own engine
description: A second app instance (npm run app:isolated, MPI-458) cannot generate: /comfy/start probes port 48188, finds the user's OWN engine answering, and returns 409 'most likely another ComfyUI - close it'. activeComfyProcess is module-level in the server fork, so it answers 'did I spawn it', not 'is an engine up'; any instance that did not spawn reads a healthy shared engine as a stranger. /comfy/status has the same defect and reports running:false while attached. The MPI-434 guard was right when the engine shared ComfyUI's default 8188 with the G:\ComfyUi bench, but the engine now owns a private 48188 and MPI-458 made a second instance routine. FIX: an answering port means attach - /comfy/start returns success, /comfy/status returns running:true. Do NOT just delete the 409: control would fall through to spawn(), a second ComfyUI would fail to bind an occupied port, and the instance ends with a DEAD engine instead of a dialog. stop/unload already no-op without activeComfyProcess, so an attached instance cannot kill the owner's engine - left alone.
